title: GCL Season 4 preview: What to expect as the world’s top players head to Bengaluru
summary: The FIDE Tech Mahindra Global Chess League is returning for its fourth season. With its unique format and competition concept, GCL is looking less like an annual chess tournament and more like a mature global sports league. After Dubai, London and Mumbai, Season 4 will take place in the southern Indian city of Bengaluru, from 5th to 13th September. With India being one of the fastest-growing chess markets and following an unprecedented response to Season 3 in Mumbai, hosting the event in the country for the second time in a row builds on strong Indian momentum in world chess. This is where the “India exports not only chess talent but also a chess format” narrative belongs. Season 4 will see Magnus Carlsen’s return to the competition. World Cup winner and India’s rising woman chess star Divya Deshmukh joins the GCL for the first time, while Viswanathan Anand moves from Ganges Grandmasters, where he spent the first three seasons, to PBG Alaskan Knights. The unusually strong generational pairings, the Road2GCL event prior to the season, a more ambitious technology/fan layer, and growing outside investment in franchises point to an exciting new GCL Season ahead. “We are very excited about Season 4 which is designed to deliver a bigger, bolder version of everything done in the previous three events. We will have a significantly larger fan-facing setup than in previous events, a more prominent technology layer with AR/VR and Physical AI, and we already have a refreshed set of teams promising exciting matchups and outcomes,” says Peeyush Dubey, Chairperson, Tech Mahindra Global Chess League. Bengaluru: Chess meets India’s technology capital Season 4 takes place in Bengaluru, marking a clear connection between chess and technology, which has been one of the staple points of GCL since inception. Dubbed “the Silicon Valley of India,” the city is home to India’s best-known tech companies, with a large population of students and tech professionals. This goes hand in hand with GCL positioning technology as a key tool in improving the spectator experience and engagement with chess. Bangalore Palace – the 19th century royal palace built for the Maharaja of Mysore – will host the opening ceremony while the competition itself will take place at The Lalit Ashok luxury hotel. Taking chess beyond the venue, GCL also continued with its Road2GCL programme which was launched in 2025 and saw online and in-person competitions. The year-round engagement platform is designed to bring players, creators, fans to celebrate chess through different events. When GCL launched four years ago featuring a franchise league structure, some doubted the chances of this approach succeeding in chess. Still, with Season 4 lined up, the league has moved from proving that franchise chess can work to building continuity. According to the analysis provided by GCL, the media reach grew 65% from Season 1 to Season 3, while the media value of the project increased 2.4 times. Magnus Carlsen’s return and Divya Deshmukh’s debut From a purely chess perspective, the biggest news of Season Four is the return of Magnus Carlsen after he skipped Season 3. The Norwegian returns as the Icon player of the Alpine APL Pipers, the defending champions of the League. It is not just Carlsen who makes Pipers the top favourites this season. The team lineup features Anish Giri and Vidit Gujrathi on Men’s Superstar boards. The Pipers also strengthened their women’s ranks, with Koneru Humpy being joined by Divya Deshmukh, the rising sensation who took the Women’s World Cup by surprise. At 19, she defeated Humpy in the FIDE Women’s World Cup final in Batumi. The victory made her the first Indian winner of the Women’s World Cup and earnt her the Grandmaster title. The Humpy – Divya tandem also tells another compelling story of GCL: two generations of elite Indian women players in the same team, highlighting that generational dynamics are also a big GCL feature. The team’s Prodigy board will be manned by Volodar Murzin, the 2024 World Rapid Chess Champion. Viswanathan Anand changes teams for Season 4 One of the most visible changes this season involves Viswanathan Anand. After representing Ganges Grandmasters for the first three editions, the five-time World Champion moves to PBG Alaskan Knights and takes their Icon board. Anand will be leading one of the youngest teams in the League: with the 15-year-old Turkish star Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus joining Arjun Erigaisi on the Superstar Men boards. Kateryna Lagno and Nino Batsiashvili fill the Superstar Women positions, while Abhimanyu Mishra (17) makes his league debut as the team’s Prodigy. Anand, therefore, enters Season 4 alongside some of the youngest players in elite chess. The other franchises have taken different approaches. Two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings have retained much of their established core, including Alireza Firouzja, Wei Yi, Alexandra Kosteniuk, and Zhu Jiner. Ganges Grandmasters have built around experience, with Ian Nepomniachtchi taking the Icon board alongside Levon Aronian and Leinier Dominguez. Mumba Masters continue with Maxime Vachier-Lagrave as their Icon, while FYERS American Gambits enter the season with World Champion Candidate Javokhir Sindarov leading a squad that also includes Daniil Dubov and Nihal Sarin. A particularly strong “old guard vs. next generation” season The generational divide is another defining characteristic of Season 4. At one end there are seasoned champions Anand, Carlsen, Aronian, Nepomniachtchi, MVL, Humpy, Kosteniuk. At the other end – rising stars: Divya, Erdogmus, Abhimanyu Mishra, Murzin, Pranav Venkatesh, Leon Mendonca, and others. The team structure of the competition means that different generations will not just be playing against or alongside one another, but they will depend on one another for the team result. Why GCL plays differently from a traditional chess tournament The competition format remains GCL’s biggest competitive differentiator. For those new to GCL, this format is the main thing to understand ahead of the event. Six franchises compete in a double round-robin league stage before the knockouts to determine the champion. title: Chess is getting its own home on the internet: FIDE and World Chess apply for the .chess domain extension
summary: The application for the game’s official top-level domain has been submitted to ICANN – the first chance in over a decade to create one. If approved, every federation, club, tournament and titled player will be able to carry a verified domain name ending in .chess.  LAUSANNE / LONDON, September 1, 2026 – The International Chess Federation (FIDE) and World Chess (LSE: CHSS), FIDE’s official commercial partner, announce that an application has been submitted to ICANN, the organisation that governs internet names, for .chess – a new top-level domain (TLD) built for the game. The application was filed in ICANN’s first new-domain window since 2012, through a dedicated subsidiary of World Chess and on behalf of FIDE. The application was submitted as a community one – this status provides it with potential leverage over any competing applications for the same string through ICANN’s Community Priority Evaluation process.  Today, the chess-related domains are scattered across .com, .org and dozens of country-code strings, and nothing marks them as belonging to the game. .chess changes that. Just as .com serves commerce, .chess will serve one game: a dedicated, officially recognised TLD where every name – be it for  a national federation or a neighbourhood club, a super-tournament or a grandmaster’s own page – is verified as genuine part of the chess world. What .chess means for the chess world National federations will receive dedicated .chess domains, allocated in coordination with FIDE – a common, recognisable internet identifier system for organised chess in every country. Clubs, academies, organisers, platforms, media and players will be able to register names that instantly say what they are: a string built for the game, backed by the institution that has governed it since 1924, and operated by World Chess. Under the agreement, FIDE acts as the institutional sponsor of the domain and receives a share of the revenues it generates, together with an allocation of domains within the TLD. World Chess manages the application, funds the project and, if the application is successful, will operate the extension on FIDE’s behalf. The initiative is a part of the broader programme by FIDE to build the sport’s digital infrastructure. First move for the community Registration will open only if and when ICANN approves the application. Ahead of that, an early-access list is open at worldchess.com/domains: members of the list will receive regular project updates, including notices of the upcoming domain registration availability, allowing them to be among the first to secure the names they are interested in. Viswanathan Anand, Interim FIDE President  “Chess deserves its own place on the internet – one where a player, a parent or a sponsor can see at a glance that a domain is genuinely part of the game. .chess will give our federations and our community a shared, trusted home online, and I am glad that FIDE is anchoring it together with World Chess.” Ilya Merenzon, CEO of World Chess “Chess has everything a major sport needs — ratings, titles, a global federation, a billion-strong audience –  everything except its own territory on the internet. .chess is that territory. Approval is not guaranteed, and ICANN’s process is rigorous. But this is infrastructure the game deserves, and together with FIDE we intend to build it – and to hand every federation, club and player a domain that says exactly who they are. FIDE – the international governing body for chess, recognised by the International Olympic Committee, with 200+ national federations – has endorsed the application as institutional sponsor. The Company’s management believes the application is strongly positioned in the Community Priority Evaluation.” For national chess federations Federations will receive further information from FIDE and World Chess about their dedicated domain names as the ICANN process advances. Questions and expressions of interest can be sent to im@worldchess.com – no action is required at this stage. You can find more information and sign up for alerts at worldchess.com/domains.  About World Chess World Chess (LSE: CHSS) is a London-based chess gaming and entertainment company and FIDE’s official commercial partner. World Chess organised the FIDE World Championship Matches in the USA and the UK and revolutionised the sport by signing the biggest media partnerships in chess history. World Chess is the creator and operator of Armageddon, the chess league for prime-time television. For more information, visit worldchess.com.
